title: Revenue de-risking & Headcount Tranching — Proposal
body:
Executive summary:

Purpose: propose a tranche-based headcount and budget protocol tied to observed pricing elasticity and early revenue signals. The goal: preserve runway under downside revenue scenarios while allowing quick re-acceleration if pricing/usage rebounds. This is a hybrid of a hiring ladder + revenue-triggered tranche release.

High-level idea: split planned new hiring and discretionary project spend for FY27 into three tranches (Green / Yellow / Red). Each tranche has release conditions tied to (a) realized price per 1M tokens (net of credits), (b) 90-day rolling ARR delta vs plan, and (c) margin/cost-per-token thresholds.

Key assumptions (base case):
- FY27 revenue plan: $120M ARR baseline at beginning of planning (assumes current pricing mix and ~35% embedded usage growth).
- Gross margin target (post-infra): 62% baseline.
- Cash runway target: >= 12 months at plan burn.
- New hires proposed for FY27 (net new headcount): 46 FTEs broken down as Eng: 24, SRE/Infra: 6, Product/PD: 6, CS/Onboarding: 6, Finance/Legal/Ops: 4.
- Typical ramp-to-productivity: 3 months for CS/PD, 6 months for Eng/SRE.
- Pricing sensitivity: elasticity assumed -0.8 for mid-market and -1.3 for price-sensitive SMB segments.

Tranche design (summary):
- Green tranche (immediate release): 40% of planned hires + 30% of discretionary spend. Conditions: current quarter revenue >= 95% of plan AND 30-day token yield (rev per 1M tokens) within -5% of baseline.
- Yellow tranche (conditional release): 35% of hires + 40% of discretionary spend. Conditions: 90-day rolling ARR >= 98% of plan OR price per 1M tokens recovered to within -2% of baseline; requires CFO + Head of Eng signoff.
- Red tranche (hold/backstop): 25% of hires + 30% discretionary spend. Conditions: only released after 2 consecutive quarters meeting baseline revenue growth trajectory OR a formal board-approved reprioritization. Otherwise funds are redeployed to runway.

Headcount phasing (proposed by tranche and quarter):
Quarter table (new hires start):
Q1: Green hires start 60% of Green tranche (~11 hires)
Q2: remaining Green hires + 40% Yellow start (~10 hires)
Q3: remaining Yellow start (~8 hires)
Q4: Red tranche conditional (deferred unless triggers met) (~7 hires)

Impact on monthly burn (approx, incremental):
- Avg fully-loaded cost per new hire: $23k / month (includes payroll, benefits, recruiting amortized, workstation, infra credits)
- Green tranche incremental burn (first 6 months): +$180k/month
- Full ramp incremental burn at steady state (46 hires): +$1.06M/month compared to base staffing

Budget sensitivity snapshots (selected lines, FY27 annualized):
Table: scenario / ARR / Gross Margin / Net Burn impact / Runway delta (months)
- Base plan: $120M / 62% / 0 incremental / 13.2 months
- Down -12% price/usage: $105.6M / 58% / +$8.3M annualized burn / runway -4.1 months
- Down -25% price/usage: $90M / 53% / +$18.9M annualized burn / runway -9.5 months
- Up +10% price/usage: $132M / 64% / -$3.5M annualized burn / runway +1.6 months

Pricing sensitivity model (concise):
- Inputs: baseline price per 1M tokens, customer mix (enterprise 30%, mid-market 45%, SMB 25%), elasticity per segment (enterprise -0.3, mid-market -0.8, SMB -1.3).
- Output: revenue delta by price change band and implied headcount delta needed to service equivalent throughput.

Example: a 15% universal price compression leads to estimated ARR -11% (weighted elasticity), with disproportionate usage increase in SMB that raises infra cost intensity; net margin falls by ~4–6 pps depending on caching/quantization adoption.

Triggers & governance (practical):
- Weekly revenue & token-yield dashboard feeds product/finance; automated flags raised when 7-day rolling revenue < 92% of plan or price per 1M drops > 8% vs baseline.
- Trigger 1 (soft): 7-day flag -> pause all non-critical contractor starts and hiring (resolve in 5 business days)
- Trigger 2 (medium): 30-day sustained drop -> freeze Yellow tranche; require 3-person review (CFO, Head of Eng, Head of Product) to rebaseline
- Trigger 3 (hard): 60-90 day sustained drop -> hold Red tranche; deploy contingency reduction playbook (two-weeks to identify discretionary spend reductions and reassign hires)

Operational notes for implementation:
- Hiring requisitions: tag hires with tranche code at requisition creation in Workday; recruiting prioritizes Green tranche roles with SLA 30 days to offer.
- Budget tracking: maintain a 'tranche ledger' in the finance model (sheet tabs: baseline, tranche-green, tranche-yellow, tranche-red) that reconciles to headcount system weekly.
- Pricing experiments: limit broad price cuts until we run 3 A/B experiments against control across representative mid-market customers; each experiment should measure both immediate revenue and 60-day retention/usage lift.

Downside mitigation levers (ordered by time-to-effect):
1) Delay Red tranche hires and freeze discretionary projects (immediate)
2) Pull forward cost-optimization from infra (quantization pilot, higher cache retention) (4–8 weeks)
3) Pricing experiments and targeted discounts instead of universal cuts (6–12 weeks)
4) Re-deploy contractors to cover critical roadmaps while delaying perm hires (4 weeks)
5) Consider temporary hiring slow-down with targeted retention bonuses for top performers if needed (board-level decision)

Quick sensitivity appendix (numbers are illustrative):
- If ARR falls to $96M (-20%), we recommend holding Yellow+Red (defer ~23 hires), realize $6.3M annual labor cost avoidance, and trigger aggressive infra cost program estimated to free $2.1M. Combined mitigation extends runway by ~5.2 months versus hold-all scenario.

Open questions & decisions needed:
- Do we adopt universal tranche tagging in Workday by Jan 1 or pilot for engineering only?
- What signal threshold should be used for enterprise vs mid-market price elasticity (we used conservative mid-market assumptions but may validate with experiments)?
- Board notification cadence for tranche holds >60 days?

Next steps (owners and timeline):
- Finance: build tranche ledger model and integrate with existing FY27 sheet (owner: Priya) — deliver by 2026-11-17
- Recruiting: create tranche-based req templates and priority routing (owner: Maya) — deliver by 2026-11-24
- Product: prepare 3 pricing experiment designs for mid-market (owner: Ethan) — deliver by 2026-12-01
- Exec: adopt tranche protocol at November finance review (owner: CFO) — decision by 2026-11-30

Appendix (attachments suggested):
- Detailed tranche ledger (tabbed sheet) with role-level cost amortization and hire-by-date
- Sensitivity workbook with elasticity knobs by segment + infra intensity maps
- Template Workday tags and recruiting SLAs

Notes to reviewers: this is an operational proposal intended to be pragmatic and conservative. The tranche percentages are adjustable and were selected to balance near-term hiring momentum with runway protection. Feedback welcome on the recommended elasticity values and the exact threshold gates for tranche release.
